content: Okay, new regressions should get issues filed to the Wasmtime repo, rather than AWFY going forward!
fitzgen (he/him) has marked this topic as resolved.
and the regression issues are working! first one on the Wasmtime repo is here: https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/issues/15192

Question for you @fitzgen (he/him), how come the results are rolled up and made for a series of commits? Does AWFY run on a fixed schedule and just benchmark whatever's there? If so, would it be possible to refactor to run for individual commits or is that expected to take too long?

With https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/issues/15210 there's both improvements and regressions from what I think are orthogonal changes, and assuming it's "just a bit of infrastructure" it'd be best I think to not need to manually sort through commits

Alex Crichton said:

how come the results are rolled up and made for a series of commits? Does AWFY run on a fixed schedule and just benchmark whatever's there? If so, would it be possible to refactor to run for individual commits or is that expected to take too long?

It runs on a cron job scheduled every 2 hours, but each benchmarking run takes up to ~2.5 hours and we limit concurrency to 1. So it just benchmarks whatever new commits are there since the last job (or doesn't benchmark anything if there are no new commits)

We could look into lifting the concurrency limit (since running the cron more frequently won't change much given that a run takes longer than the scheduled interval) but then we also have to figure out how to merge automatically results better, since a previous run won't have finished and been committed before we kick off the next run. And the data for runs is stored in incrementing ID directories...

Also not sure we want to burn more of our CI time on this or not.

What I've been doing when there is a regression range is try to bisect locally to figure out which exact commit(s) are responsible. I guess we could also look into automating the bisect?

It seems like (with the baseline assumption that building infra is easier now than it would have been otherwise) a bisect that only runs the benchmarks that showed statistical movement in the rollup run would be both useful, and much faster/cheaper. Maybe even as simple as: for any run with movement, spawn off sub-runs for every contained commit individually (N against N-1 in the linear history) just for the benchmarks the moved.

That does have the potential to miss a benchmark that moved one way in commit N then exactly canceled out in N+1 in the rollup, but for most common cases of "two different orthogonal signals are contained here" it seems cheap and easy (in terms of CI time)?

Usage-wise a full CI run in the wasmtime repo is 22h worth of minutes, so adding 2 to that for each commit doesn't seem like it'd really radically change usage all that much. 2.5h of benchmarking for each commit is indeed quite weighty though...

Infrastructure-wise the way I'd imagine it is that a cron sees what new commits are available and then there's a job of "hey benchmark this commit" and triggers that for each commit, and then the parallelism isn't capped for "benchmark this commit". I'd ideally like to one day have the workflow for "leave a comment on a PR and get a benchmark summary" and this might be a step towards that perhaps.

With a little sharding across parallel jobs, I think I can get a full benchmark run to take about an hour. This will let us speed up the frequency of scheduling to narrow ranges benchmarked as well.

I'm also investigating automating a parallel bisect that runs only the regressing benchmarks, which should give us precise commit blame in ~15-60 minutes depending on the benchmarks that regressed.
